_doc: Repo-local Claude Code settings for RytmRandomizer.
The hooks block below auto-invokes the code-reviewer agent after a git
push. The matcher fires PostToolUse on any Bash invocation whose command
begins with `git push`. The harness invokes the agent definition at
.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md, which runs the 8-step code-review skill
at .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md (Steps 7-8 add abstraction-reuse
analysis and architecture-doc/diagram freshness).
SETUP — no action needed. Claude Code reads .claude/settings.json
automatically from the repo root. Codex has its own equivalent at
.codex/hooks.json (also zero-setup). A universal git pre-push hook at
.githooks/pre-push runs the mechanical gates for ANY tool once
core.hooksPath is set (`just install` / the dev container do this).
All three call the one shared scripts/code_review_gate.py. See
docs/CODE_REVIEW_HOOK_SETUP.md for the full three-mechanism picture
and what to do if the harness does not support the `Agent` action.
If your harness version does not yet support the `Agent` action type for
hooks, the hook is ignored harmlessly. Run the review manually with
`/agent code-reviewer` or `/skill code-review` (Claude Code), or per
docs/CODE_REVIEW_HOOK_SETUP.md (codex / other agents). The review is
ALSO enforced server-side by the `architecture` CI job, so a skipped
local hook never lets a violation merge.
See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and .claude/rules/architecture.md for the
architecture spec that the code-reviewer agent enforces.

action.prompt: A `git push` just completed in this worktree. Execute the code-review skill (.claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md) against the most recently pushed commits. Gather the diff with `git log --oneline -10` plus `git diff @{upstream}..HEAD` (or `git diff <base-branch>...HEAD` if no upstream). Run the review as ONE TARGETED AGENT PER DIMENSION, in parallel — not one wide agent covering everything — per the skill's 'Execution model' section: spawn separate agents for architecture/import-direction, house style/type hygiene, parity + test hygiene, side effects + mido leakage, observability, abstraction reuse/genericization (Step 7: could the new code be generalized, or does an existing abstraction such as the Device Protocol, the snapshot envelope helpers, the generic senders, cli_registry, data/, observability/metrics, or the report formatter already cover it), and docs + diagram freshness (Step 8: are docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAMS.md updated for any architecture-surface change, and do the quoted counts still match). Each dimension agent runs `pytest tests/architecture/ -q` as needed. Then synthesize the per-dimension findings into ONE structured Critical/Important/Minor/Abstraction/Docs verdict.
